questions.question: Which of the following is the primary reason for the development of unconventional machining (UCM) processes?

options.A: Machining of soft materials only
options.B: Machining of high-strength, high-hardness and heat-resistant materials, and complex shapes

questions.question: Thermo-electric energy based UCM processes include:

options.A: AJM, WJM
options.C: EDM, WEDM, LBM, PAM, EBM, IBM

questions.question: Which mechanism of material removal is common to EDM, LBM and EBM?

options.A: Mechanical erosion

questions.question: A component made of tungsten carbide (hard, brittle, electrically conductive) needs a complex 3-D cavity. Which UCM process is most suitable?

options.A: USM

questions.question: Unconventional machining processes are generally preferred over conventional machining when:

options.A: The material is soft and ductile
options.B: Material hardness/strength is very high or the shape is intricate
options.D: Production rate must be maximised at lowest cost

questions.question: In the classification of UCM processes by mechanism of material removal, EDM belongs to which category?

options.A: Mechanical

questions.question: In EDM, material removal takes place due to:

options.A: Electrochemical dissolution
options.B: Erosion caused by repetitive spark discharges

questions.question: The dielectric fluid used in EDM performs all of the following functions EXCEPT:

options.A: Insulation between electrode and workpiece
options.D: Increasing electrical conductivity between electrode and workpiece

questions.question: In an EDM process, the spark frequency is 4000 sparks/s and the MRR is 800 mm³/min. The average volume of metal removed per spark is approximately:
Which of the following materials CANNOT be machined by conventional EDM?

options.A: Hardened steel

questions.question: For achieving a higher metal removal rate (roughing cuts) in EDM, which polarity setting is typically used?

options.A: Workpiece positive, tool negative (straight polarity)
options.D: Polarity has no effect on MRR

questions.question: Tool electrode materials commonly used in EDM include all of the following EXCEPT:

options.A: Copper

questions.question: "Overcut" in EDM refers to:

options.A: The difference between electrode size and machined cavity size due to spark gap
options.D: Extra time taken to machine the component

questions.question: If the discharge energy per spark in EDM is 2 × 10⁻³ J and the spark frequency is 10,000 Hz, the average power input is:
Which of the following is a genuine advantage of EDM?

options.A: Can machine any hard, electrically conductive material irrespective of hardness
options.B: Gives the highest MRR of all machining processes

questions.question: A major limitation of the EDM process is that:

options.A: It can machine only electrically conductive materials
options.C: It requires very high cutting forces

questions.question: The dielectric commonly used in die-sinking EDM is:

options.A: Kerosene or EDM oil

questions.question: The gap maintained between the tool and workpiece during EDM is generally of the order of:
Tool Wear Ratio (TWR) in EDM is defined as:

options.A: Volume of tool wear / Volume of work material removed
options.B: Volume of work material removed / Volume of tool wear

questions.question: The servo control system in an EDM machine is primarily used to:

options.A: Maintain a constant spark gap between tool and workpiece

questions.question: In Wire EDM, the tool electrode is:

options.A: A stationary shaped block

questions.question: Commonly used wire electrode materials in WEDM include:

options.A: Brass and molybdenum

questions.question: The dielectric medium generally used in WEDM is:

options.A: Deionised water

questions.question: WEDM is particularly suitable for machining:

options.A: Complex 2-D profiles/contours in conductive, hard materials

questions.question: In WEDM, wire tension during cutting is typically maintained:

options.A: High, but below the breaking strength of the wire
options.C: Above the breaking strength of the wire
options.D: Tension is irrelevant to the process

questions.question: A key advantage of WEDM over conventional (ram/die-sinking) EDM is:

options.A: No pre-shaped tool electrode is required — the wire itself acts as the tool
options.C: It gives a much higher MRR than milling
options.D: It does not need a dielectric fluid

questions.question: A recognised limitation of WEDM is:

options.A: It is a relatively slow process compared to conventional cutting
options.B: It can cut only soft materials

questions.question: WEDM finds application in the manufacture of:

options.A: Press-tool dies, punches and extrusion dies with intricate profiles

questions.question: Laser Beam Machining removes material primarily by:

options.A: Melting and vaporisation caused by a focused, high-intensity coherent light beam

questions.question: Laser types commonly used in LBM are:

options.A: CO₂ and Nd:YAG lasers

questions.question: A laser beam of power 500 W is focused to a spot of diameter 0.1 mm. The approximate power density at the focal spot is:
LBM is best suited for:

options.A: Small holes and fine cuts in hard, brittle and heat-resistant materials
options.D: Underwater cutting of thick steel plates

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a process parameter affecting LBM performance?

options.A: Laser power

questions.question: A major advantage of LBM is that it is:

options.A: A non-contact process with no tool wear, capable of very small/precise features
options.B: Suited to very high bulk MRR
options.D: Equally effective regardless of material reflectivity

questions.question: A recognised limitation of LBM is:

options.A: Formation of a heat-affected zone (HAZ) and recast layer

questions.question: In LBM, an assist gas (e.g. oxygen, nitrogen, compressed air) is mainly used to:

options.A: Blow away molten/vaporised material and assist the cutting action

questions.question: Typical applications of LBM include:

options.A: Micro-hole drilling in turbine blades, PCB cutting and semiconductor scribing
options.C: Deep-hole drilling of gun barrels only

questions.question: The Nd:YAG laser is preferred for many LBM applications because it:

options.A: Emits near-infrared radiation (~1.06 µm) that is well absorbed by metals and can be pulsed for precision drilling
options.B: Emits only visible red light for cosmetic marking
options.C: Operates in the microwave range for deep penetration
options.D: Operates in the X-ray range for imaging only

questions.question: Plasma Arc Machining uses a high-temperature ionised gas jet that typically attains temperatures of:
Plasma in PAM is generated by:

options.A: Ionising a gas passed through a DC electric arc between electrode and nozzle

questions.question: Gases commonly used to generate plasma in PAM include:

options.A: Argon, nitrogen and hydrogen (or their mixtures)

questions.question: PAM is primarily used for:

options.A: Cutting electrically conductive metals, especially stainless steel and aluminium plates

questions.question: Compared to oxy-fuel flame cutting, plasma arc cutting has the advantage that it can:

options.A: Cut non-ferrous metals and stainless steels which oxy-fuel cannot cut effectively
options.D: Offer no advantage over oxy-fuel cutting

questions.question: A disadvantage of PAM compared to EDM/LBM is:

options.A: A wider heat-affected zone and lower dimensional accuracy
options.B: Inability to cut metal thicker than 1 mm
options.C: Inability to be used for underwater cutting

questions.question: The two main types of plasma arc processes are:

options.A: Transferred-arc and non-transferred-arc plasma

questions.question: In transferred-arc PAM, the workpiece acts as:

options.A: One of the electrodes, becoming part of the electrical circuit for higher energy concentration
options.B: An insulator not connected to the circuit

questions.question: In Electron Beam Machining, material removal occurs because:

options.A: The kinetic energy of high-velocity electrons converts to heat on impact, causing melting/vaporisation
options.B: Electrons react chemically with the workpiece

questions.question: EBM is generally carried out inside:

options.A: A high-vacuum chamber, to prevent scattering of electrons by air molecules
options.B: The open atmosphere, to reduce cost

questions.question: In EBM, electrons are accelerated through a potential difference of 150 kV. The kinetic energy gained by each electron is:
Typical accelerating voltage used in EBM lies in the range of:

options.A: 50 kV to 200 kV

questions.question: EBM is best suited for:

options.A: Drilling very fine, high-aspect-ratio micro-holes in thin sheets/foils
options.B: Bulk removal of large volumes of metal
options.C: Machining non-metallic insulators without any conductive coating

questions.question: A major limitation of EBM is:

options.A: High equipment cost and the need for a vacuum chamber, which limits workpiece size
options.B: Its inability to achieve fine tolerances
options.C: Its inability to machine refractory metals
options.D: It always produces a very large heat-affected zone

questions.question: The electron beam in EBM is focused using:

options.A: Electromagnetic lenses

questions.question: Typical applications of EBM include:

options.A: Micro-drilling of turbine-blade cooling holes, electron-beam welding and fine slitting

questions.question: In Ion Beam Machining, material removal occurs mainly through:

options.A: Sputtering — momentum transfer from bombarding ions knocking off surface atoms

questions.question: Ion Beam Machining is typically characterised by:

options.A: Atomic/nanometre-scale removal rates, used for ultra-precision surface finishing
options.B: Very high MRR suitable for bulk shaping
options.C: Operation at atmospheric pressure without vacuum

questions.question: The gas commonly ionised to produce the ion beam in IBM is:

options.A: Argon (an inert gas)

questions.question: IBM is widely applied for:

options.A: Thinning of semiconductor wafers, photomask repair, and figuring of optical mirror surfaces

questions.question: A key advantage of IBM is:

options.A: Extremely high precision (atomic-level) material removal with minimal thermal/mechanical damage

questions.question: A major limitation of IBM is:

options.A: Extremely low material removal rate and high (vacuum) equipment cost, limiting it to small precision work
options.D: Inability to achieve fine surface finish
